COMPLIANCE AND RECORDKEEPING POLICY

1. Customer Due Diligence
The institution must perform customer due diligence before establishing
a lending relationship. Customer identity and relevant customer information
must be verified in accordance with applicable compliance requirements.

2. Anti-Money Laundering Controls
Customer and transaction activity must be reviewed for indicators of
potential money laundering or other suspicious activity. Identified concerns
must be handled through the institution's established reporting procedures.

suspicious activity. Identified concerns
must be handled through the institution's established reporting procedures.

3. Auditability
Credit application records must retain identity verification findings,
repayment capacity calculations, and credit-history review outcomes.
Records must provide sufficient evidence to reconstruct the decisions made
during the credit assessment process.

4. Access and Confidentiality
Customer information must only be accessed by personnel with an authorized
business need. Customer records must be protected against unauthorized
disclosure, alteration, or loss.

5. Compliance Monitoring
Compliance personnel must periodically assess adherence to internal
procedures and applicable regulatory obligations. Material compliance
findings must be documented and escalated through the appropriate channels.

CREDIT POLICY

1. Borrower Eligibility
All loan applicants must provide valid government-issued photo identification.
Applicants must meet the institution's minimum eligibility requirements before
a credit application can proceed.

2. Repayment Capacity Assessment
Credit officers must assess monthly disposable income after existing debt
obligations. The maximum permitted debt-service ratio is 40 percent.
Applicants exceeding this threshold must not receive standard loan approval
without an authorized exception.

3. Credit History Review
Credit officers must review the applicant's credit history, including
unresolved defaults and delinquent repayment accounts. Adverse credit
information must be considered when determining borrower risk.

and delinquent repayment accounts. Adverse credit
information must be considered when determining borrower risk.

4. Credit Approval
Applications meeting the eligibility, repayment capacity, and credit-history
requirements may proceed through the standard approval workflow. Exceptions
must follow the institution's designated escalation and approval procedures.

GENERAL OFFICE PROCEDURES

1. Meeting Room Reservations
Employees should reserve meeting rooms through the internal scheduling
system. Reservations should include the meeting title, expected attendance,
date, and duration.

2. Office Equipment
Employees should report faulty office equipment to the facilities team.
Equipment maintenance requests must include the equipment location and
a description of the reported problem.

3. Visitor Management
Visitors must register at the reception desk upon arrival. Hosts are
responsible for notifying reception when their visitors have arrived.

4. Office Supplies
Departments may request stationery and other office supplies through
the standard procurement process. Requests should identify the items
required and the intended department.

5. Workplace Communication
Employees should use approved internal communication channels for routine
administrative announcements and workplace coordination.

LOAN OPERATIONS STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE

1. Application Registration
Every loan application must be assigned a unique application reference.
Operations personnel must record the applicant's details, submission date,
requested loan amount, and application status.

2. Document Verification
Operations personnel must confirm that all required application documents
have been received. Identity documents must be checked for completeness and
consistency with the information submitted by the applicant.

3. Application Processing
Applications with missing documentation must be returned for clarification.
Applications with complete documentation may proceed to credit assessment.
The application status must be updated at every major processing stage.

4. Loan Disbursement
Approved loan applications may proceed to disbursement after all required
approval conditions have been satisfied. Disbursement records must include
the approved amount, transaction reference, and disbursement date.

5. Record Retention
Application records and supporting documents must be retained in accordance
with the institution's records-management requirements.

RISK MANAGEMENT POLICY

1. Risk Identification
The institution must identify and document risks arising from lending
activities. Risk assessments should consider borrower characteristics,
repayment capacity, credit history, and relevant external factors.

2. Risk Classification
Credit applications must be classified according to the institution's
approved risk categories. Risk classifications must be supported by
documented assessment findings.

3. Exception Escalation
Applications that fall outside established credit policy thresholds must be
escalated to the senior credit approval committee when the applicable
delegated authority requires committee review.

escalated to the senior credit approval committee when the applicable

4. Approval Authority
Credit officers may approve applications only within their assigned
delegated approval limits. Applications exceeding those limits require
approval from the appropriate higher authority.

5. Risk Monitoring
The risk management function must periodically review lending portfolio
performance, identify emerging risks, and report significant findings to
management.
